english.title: Conspire to commit indictable / either way offence outside England and Wales in relation to immigration offences
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) conspired together with

(A)_[**(..SPECIFY THE PERSON..)]_
(B)_[**(..SPECIFY THE PERSONS..)]_
(C)_[another person]_
(D)_[other persons]_

(E)_[offence of **(..SPECIFY OFFENCE..)]_
(F)_[offences of **(..SPECIFY OFFENCES..)]_

english.legislation: Contrary to sections 1, 1A and 3 of the Criminal Law Act 1977
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
conspired with one or more persons
to commit an offence in relation to immigration
outside England and Wales

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) This offence should only be used where the conspiracy is to commit immigration offences OUTSIDE OF England and Wales.
(ii) Section 1A of the Criminal Law Act 1977, as amended by section 72 of the Coroners and Justice Act 2009, provides conditions in relation to this offence.
(iii) Section 1 of the Criminal Law Act 1977 provides the offence of conspiracy. The ingredients of the statutory offence of conspiracy were set out at length in R v Saik 2006.
